title: FR-5's first acceptance: pH-conditioned transfer, damage, leak and reseal on an owned compartment, in two arms on FR-4's steady state
status: PROPOSED (drafted 15 November 2026 by the FR-4/FR-5 physics owner on branch fr45-physics). It stays PROPOSED until the integrated candidate runs; registration is the lead's, after the dt study and a rehearsal. The arm values and restated claims are confirmed by the references' readout (branch 931fb38a; compartment-transfer-arms-01-readout.* beside /mnt/workspaces/Cells/independent-references-20261115-01/compartment-transfer-arms-01/), which reran the record's own worlds and reproduced it exactly

registration.no_judged_run_yet: No run of either arm exists: the core's insertion points and this branch's laws are not yet wired
registration.path: The lead registers it from a clean snapshot of the integrated candidate, after this protocol's dt study and a rehearsal (the D150/MG0c path); it travels with fr45-physics's merge into integration-d172
registration.launch: each judged unit through scripts/run_detached.sh, --oom-first, cap 2G unless a development run measures more

rung: FR-5, acceptance 1 (numerical verification, D174's first claim kind; no living-cell claim)
question: On FR-4's steady state, does the engine move a neutral cargo across the bounding patch only while the compartment is in its declared condition (arm T), release it through a damage pore when the patch is injured and recover after resealing (arm R), with every book closed, agreement with the independent reference within X's budget, and controls that fail by at least ten times that budget?
engine_models: resolved_pump_tissue@3 with the core's stage-read, transporter, held-row and face-free-term insertion points
passive_neutral_permeation@1 (the conditioned transfer and the cargo pore)
bounding_patch_damage@1 (the damage control state, exact per step)
ph_conditioned_factor@1 (the condition, through the routing door)
the coupling operator's routing door (the factors' multiply), and cell_owned_compartments@1
scope: FR-4's scope (maintained fuel, the K+ counterion, a lumped population of 1000 as declared, fixed volume, explicit ARS(2,2,2)), plus FR-5's damage, a proton pore and a neutral cargo pore. Ionic pores are refused in version 1 (they wait for the implicit patch). The single-compartment form is reported, not judged
driver: validation/compartment_ph/definitions.py fr5_world(parameters.ARM_T or ARM_R), run by the dt-study harness once wired

start.declared: FR-4's engine checkpoint at t = 1800 s of fr4_world(World()), its steady state (pH_L about 5.0946 per the references); FR-5's t = 0 is that checkpoint, with X added at its declared start amounts
start.reference: REQUIRED for X's budget: the reference starts from the engine's own 1800 s checkpoint (tr.Start), not a recomputed steady state. X_L along the run moves by about 0.06 B per 1e-3 pH of start offset (the references' readout)

T.claim: X crosses while the lumen is acidic. A proton-only damage raises pH_L above pH50, and while pH_L > pH50 the conditioned transfer's mean rate falls at least 10-fold below its mean rate over the pre-damage interval, judged on the route's cumulative transfer in units of X's budget B (the rerun measured about 14-fold: 152 B over 74-326 s against 497 B in the 59 s before damage). After resealing, pH_L returns below pH50 before 400 s, with the crossing time within 5 s of the reference's (327 s in the rerun), and the transfer resumes.
T.control: f = 1 (no condition): X keeps crossing through the alkaline window; the lumen's X and the conditioned route's cumulative transfer differ from arm T by at least 10x X's budget
T.confirmed: 8.375 B/s over [0, 60] s against 0.6120 B/s over [73.081, 326.882] s (ratio 13.69 >= 10); pH_L above pH50 at 73.081 s, back below at 326.882 s

R.claim: The slow conditioned route keeps most X in the lumen until damage. The damage opens the cargo pore and the proton pore, giving a release burst (at least 0.8 of X_L(0) released inside the window; the rerun measured 0.874) and a pH rise. After resealing, pH_L returns below pH50 before 400 s, with the crossing time within 5 s of the reference's (367 s in the rerun).
R.control: d = 0 (no damage): no burst and no pH rise; the lumen's X differs from arm R by at least 10x X's budget
R.confirmed: 0.8736 of X_L(0) released over [100, 160] s (>= 0.8); pH_L above pH50 at 113.081 s, back below at 366.882 s; the conditioned route carries nothing while pH_L > pH50, since the burst has already equalised X

budgets.X: |X_L,engine - X_L,reference| <= 1e-3 of the lumen's initial X at every record; the conditioned route's cumulative transfer within 1e-3 x X_L(0) x V_L (fmol). Basis: the declared physical accuracy, as FR-4's J3 and J4; the references' floor shows they resolve it
budgets.controls_margin: each control differs from its arm by at least 10x the X budget on the same quantities (G1 exact contract tests plus G3 scientific negative controls, D176)

criteria.J1_admission: both arms and their controls admitted and run without refusal at every rung
criteria.J2_orders: the dt study's observed orders in [1.8, 2.2] on the three finest rungs, for the lumen's X, the lumen's pH, V_b and the damage d
criteria.J3_state_error: at the declared 0.5 ms, the Richardson-estimated error of the lumen's X <= the X budget and of the lumen's pH <= 1e-3
criteria.J4_reference: the X and pH budgets above, against the reference started at tr.Start
criteria.J5_envelope: the closure's state-dependent envelope (rapid_proton_buffer.lag_estimate_ph <= 1e-3 pH) at every stage of every buffered node, including through the damage window
criteria.J6_protons: H_eq conserved except across routes: the change of H_eq at each node equals the sum of its routes' proton transfers (pump, leak, proton pore) to the material floor, at every record
criteria.J7_energy: the energy identity at every record: stored change + heat = the maintenance's supplied work, within FR-4's ledger tolerance; each passive route's heat >= 0
criteria.J8_cargo: X conserved across lumen, cytosol and bath to its floor; whatever leaves the lumen arrives in the cytosol on the same route
criteria.J9_bands: the cytosol's pH within its fuel band (7.2 +- 0.05) at every stage; d within [0, 1]; f within [0, 1]
criteria.J10_controls: both controls caught with the 10x margin
criteria.J11_claims: arm T's numeric claim (the >= 10-fold mean-rate reduction while pH_L > pH50) and both arms' return below pH50 before 400 s within 5 s of the reference's crossing time; arm R's release fraction >= 0.8

dt_study_criteria_written_first.note: the patch total's max-side dt x G/C_b is about 0.048 at the coarsest rung (1 ms) and 0.024 at the declared 0.5 ms; the coarsest rung sits at the world's 0.05 on purpose, as FR-4's does
checks: state error at 1 ms as J3
energy residual <= 2e-3 at 1 ms, falling at second order
the envelope as J5 on every rung
dt_study_criteria_written_first.verdict: the declared 1 ms stands if every check holds; otherwise the arm declares the finest rung that passes, reported, not repaired

recording_rules: Keep conserved proton equivalents (H_eq, the stored row) apart from free h and pH (the closure's algebraic read): report both, judge J6 on H_eq and J4's pH on the read
Keep the closure's envelope (a validity check of a reduced representation) apart from the energy and heat closure (a ledger): J5 and J7 are separate parts
Keep maintained fuel apart from depletion and recovery: like FR-4's, this world's held fuel claims neither
The lumped compartment is a deterministic continuum model, not a stochastic mean: no claim about individual compartments or their variance
reported_not_judged: compile time, memory and cost per step
the steady and peak pH values themselves (generic parameters, not claims)
what_it_does_not_show: ionic pores, Cl- counterions or the implicit patch
a damaged minority within the lumped population (that needs the population split into two compartments, §9)
disclosures: The arm values were chosen after the references' first run (R-transfer from FR-4's state at 900 s; /mnt/workspaces/Cells/independent-references-20261115-01/compartment-transfer-crosschecks-01/, and validation/compartment_ph/REFERENCES_USAGE.md) showed the original world could show neither claim: X had crossed before the damage, and the condition never closed

P_X = 1e-10 m/s for arm R comes from the references' grid; the proton pore at 1e-5 m/s (not their 1e-4) was chosen by host-side steady-state arithmetic so that both arms stay explicit at 1 ms; whether the pH crosses pH50 within each window is for their rerun to confirm

The world declares 1e-9 mM traces where a row does not apply; the references use exact zeros for the absent buffer. A declared difference: the closure's mask keys on declared (node, row) pairs, so the traces are never live buffers
The start (FR-4's checkpoint at 1800 s) was fixed after the references found FR-4's 900 s state 1.4e-3 pH from steady state, beyond the 1e-3 budget

After the references' rerun of both arms (references branch 071ef983; /mnt/workspaces/Cells/independent-references-20261115-01/compartment-transfer-arms-01/): arm T's original claim, that the transfer stops, did not hold. The route slows about 14-fold while pH_L > pH50 but does not stop, since most of the transfer happens while f passes through its half-open range, and longer windows do not change that. So the claim is restated numerically (at least 10-fold), not sharpened by parameters. The re-acidification claim is restated as a return below pH50 before 400 s, with no longer horizon. The step bound was declared on the patch total after the rerun measured 0.048 at 1 ms, so FR-5's step became 0.5 ms

The restated claims and the arm values were confirmed by the references' readout (branch 931fb38a; compartment-transfer-arms-01-readout.* beside /mnt/workspaces/Cells/independent-references-20261115-01/compartment-transfer-arms-01/), which reran the record's own worlds and reproduced it exactly, before registration and before any engine run

development_runs.note: no run of either arm; the charged-patch test's runs (fr45/charged_patch/) are development evidence for the explicit limit only

outcome_rules: PASS when J1-J10 hold for both arms; otherwise the failing criteria are reported with their values, without repair or retuning after the judged run
step_bound: The world's 0.05 (max-side dt x G/C_b) applies to the patch total, the sum over every route on the bounding patch, since those routes share one charge mode (V_b). The rerun measured the patch total at 0.048 at 1 ms at the stiffest state (the proton pore 0.029, the leak, K+). So FR-5 declares dt = 0.5 ms (patch total about 0.024, FR-4's factor-of-two margin). Price: 400 s is 8e5 steps per run instead of 4e5, about 0.8 CPU-hours per run at the charged-patch test's upper-bound cost.
